D: A shy shop assistant told she has weeks to live blows her savings on a luxury holiday in a grand European hotel.
P: Serve the main when Georgia orders everything Chef Didier makes.
S: Georgia's crab cakes with lemon aioli
Panko crumbed crab cakes with spring onion and lemon aioli

Crisp golden crab cakes packed with crab, spring onion and lemon, served with a garlicky lemon aioli and a little herb salad. Mix 400g crab meat with 3 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 egg, 2 sliced spring onions, the zest of 1 lemon, 1 tsp Dijon and 60g panko. Shape into 12 small cakes and chill 30 minutes. Roll in 60g more panko and fry in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat for 3 minutes a side. Mix 100g mayonnaise with 1 crushed garlic clove and lemon juice. Serve with the aioli and a few dressed rocket and parsley leaves.
Grandhotel Pupp mushroom and gruyère tarts
Puff pastry squares with garlicky mushrooms and gruyère

Little puff pastry tarts topped with garlic and thyme mushrooms, melted gruyère and a drizzle of truffle oil. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into 16 squares, score a 1cm border on each and prick the middle. Fry 300g sliced mixed mushrooms in 30g butter with 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme for 6 minutes until golden. Spoon onto the pastry centres and top with 100g grated gruyère. Brush the borders with egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Drizzle with a few drops of truffle oil.
M: Chef Didier's duck with orange sauce
Crisp-skinned duck breast with orange honey sauce and potatoes

Crisp-skinned pan-roasted duck breast with a glossy orange and orange liqueur sauce, potatoes fried in duck fat and green beans. Score the skin of 4 duck breasts and season. Place skin-side down in a cold pan and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes to render the fat, then flip and roast at 200C for 6 minutes. Rest. Fry 800g par-boiled diced potatoes in 3 tbsp of the duck fat until crisp. Pour off the rest of the fat, add the juice of 3 oranges, 2 tbsp honey, 30ml orange liqueur and 200ml chicken stock and reduce until glossy. Whisk in 20g butter. Serve with green beans.
W: Rich dark chocolate mousse with whipped cream

Light, rich dark chocolate mousse in little glasses with whipped cream, fresh raspberries and a crisp tuile or wafer on top. Melt 200g dark chocolate with 30g butter and cool slightly. Whisk in 3 egg yolks one at a time. Whip 200ml thickened cream to soft peaks and fold in. Whisk 3 egg whites with 40g caster sugar to soft peaks and fold through gently in two batches. Spoon into 4 glasses and chill 3 hours. Top with whipped cream, raspberries and a thin wafer biscuit.
K: Sugar cube, bitters and brandy topped with champagne

A classic champagne cocktail: a bitters-soaked sugar cube and a dash of brandy topped with champagne and an orange twist. Sparkling apple for non-drinkers. Place a sugar cube in each of 4 champagne flutes and soak it with 2 dashes of aromatic bitters. Add 15ml brandy to each glass. Slowly top with chilled champagne or sparkling wine, about 120ml per glass, and watch the bubbles rise from the sugar. Twist a strip of orange peel over each glass and drop it in.
